summary: Service oriented architecture: React + Vite SPA with Go net/http with chi and Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL on Google Cloud Run in europe-west1. Driven mainly by project.type and requirements.realtime; about $300-910/month.

architecture.justification: A devops engineer and a team of 5 can run a separate service for realtime with 5,000 concurrent users, which scales differently from the main API.

alternatives.why_not: Needs 12+ people, a devops engineer, 1,000,000+ users and scalability priority 4+; here team.size is 5, scale.users_12_months is 50,000.

frontend.justification: React + Vite SPA: largest ecosystem of canvas and shared-editor libraries for a collaborative app; the screens sit behind sign-in and need no search indexing, so a client-rendered app served as static files is enough and there is no rendering server to run; suited to project.type realtime_collab; handles the 50,000 users expected in 12 months (about 5,000 concurrent at peak); mature and well documented for a team of 5 with a devops engineer. Largest ecosystem and talent pool.

alternatives.why_not: React + Vite SPA is preferred because the screens sit behind sign-in and need no search indexing, so a client-rendered app served as static files is enough and there is no rendering server to run.
React + Vite SPA is preferred because it has the largest ecosystem of canvas and shared-editor libraries for a collaborative app.

tradeoffs: Client-side rendering hurts SEO and first load
Routing and data fetching are your choice

backend.justification: Go net/http with chi: has built-in real-time support; meets the 100 ms p95 target; handles the 50,000 users expected in 12 months (about 5,000 concurrent at peak). Compiled single binary with tiny memory footprint.

alternatives.why_not: Fastify (Node.js) scores lower on performance (3.0 against 5.0, priorities.performance is 5), worth 9.1 weighted points, more than its 2.8-point overall deficit (it gains some back on maintainability).
Supabase Cloud scores lower on performance (1.0 against 5.0, priorities.performance is 5), worth 18.2 weighted points, more than its 8.5-point overall deficit (it gains some back on time to market).
Excluded: its API routes need Next.js as the web frontend.

tradeoffs: You build auth, ORM and admin yourself
Fewer batteries than Django or Rails

database.justification: Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL: a relational database suits the data: requirements.consistency is strong; handles the 50,000 users expected in 12 months (about 5,000 concurrent at peak); mature and well documented for a team of 5 with a devops engineer. ACID transactions, JSONB, full-text search, PostGIS and pgvector in one engine. Deployed in europe-west1.

alternatives.why_not: Cloud SQL for MySQL scores lower on security (4.0 against 5.0, priorities.security is 3), worth 2.7 weighted points, more than its 2.6-point overall deficit (it gains some back on time to market).
Azure SQL Database scores lower on maintainability (4.4 against 4.7, priorities.maintainability is 4), which accounts for 1.1 of the 1.3-point gap.
Excluded: a single-writer file database cannot take 1,500 requests per second (about 100 is its limit with writes queued behind one writer).

tradeoffs: Vertical scaling first; sharding needs extra tooling
Self-managed HA and backups take skill

hosting.justification: Google Cloud Run: handles the 50,000 users expected in 12 months (about 5,000 concurrent at peak); mature and well documented for a team of 5 with a devops engineer. Any container, scales to zero, and bills per request. Deployed in europe-west1. The built React + Vite SPA web app is served from the same host as the Go net/http with chi API, so there is one deployment target.

alternatives.why_not: Azure Container Apps scores lower on maintainability (3.7 against 4.5, priorities.maintainability is 4), which accounts for 3.1 of the 4.0-point gap.

alternatives.choice: Amazon ECS on AWS Fargate with ALB
alternatives.why_not: Amazon ECS on AWS Fargate with ALB scores lower on cost (3.2 against 5.0, priorities.cost is 2), which accounts for 3.4 of the 3.9-point gap.

supporting.justification: Firebase Authentication: same cloud (Google Cloud) as the core stack, so one account and no cross-vendor traffic; handles the 50,000 users expected in 12 months (about 5,000 concurrent at peak); mature and well documented for a team of 5 with a devops engineer. Phone OTP, social and email sign-in with mobile SDKs. Deployed in us.

alternatives.why_not: Keycloak self-hosted: self-hosted, so the devops engineer must patch, scale and back it up when a managed option exists.
Firebase Authentication is preferred because same cloud (Google Cloud) as the core stack, so one account and no cross-vendor traffic.
Excluded: does not provide social sign-in.

tradeoffs: User data is processed in the US, so it fails India and EU residency
Free tier limits apply: Free tier: 50,000 MAU on Identity Platform; phone SMS billed separately.

supporting.justification: Stripe: handles recurring per-seat subscriptions; handles the 50,000 users expected in 12 months (about 5,000 concurrent at peak). Best-in-class API, Connect for marketplaces and Billing for subscriptions. Deployed in eu.

alternatives.why_not: Paddle scores lower on performance (1.0 against 3.0, priorities.performance is 5), worth 9.1 weighted points, more than its 7.0-point overall deficit.
Adyen scores lower on performance (1.0 against 3.0, priorities.performance is 5), which accounts for 9.1 of the 13.2-point gap.
Excluded: Cashfree Payments does not list gdpr_dpa in the knowledge base (required by the compliance setting).

tradeoffs: New Indian businesses can only join by invitation
Data is not stored in India, so RBI localisation fails

supporting.justification: Hocuspocus self-hosted: built for shared documents with live cursors (CRDT); runs as one more container on the chosen host and stores documents in the stack's own database, so no extra vendor holds user content; suited to project.type realtime_collab; handles the 50,000 users expected in 12 months (about 5,000 concurrent at peak); mature and well documented for a team of 5 with a devops engineer. Open-source CRDT collaboration with a self-hosted websocket server. Self-hosted although the deployment is managed_cloud: team.has_devops is true, so the team can run it. Deployed in europe-west1.

alternatives.why_not: Hocuspocus self-hosted is preferred because it is built for shared documents with live cursors (CRDT).
Hocuspocus self-hosted is preferred because it is built for shared documents with live cursors (CRDT).
Excluded: needs a library for the chosen backend language.

alternatives.why_not: Google Cloud Storage is preferred because same cloud (Google Cloud) as the core stack, so one account and no cross-vendor traffic.

supporting.justification: Resend: handles the 50,000 users expected in 12 months (about 5,000 concurrent at peak); quick to build with for a 12-week MVP. Developer-friendly email API with React Email templates. Deployed in eu-west-1.

alternatives.why_not: Twilio SendGrid and Resend are about equal on the weighted score; Resend is chosen on its free-tier terms (Free plan: 3,000 emails per month, 100 per day); Twilio SendGrid has no free tier.
Postmark: adds another vendor (Postmark) to sign up with, secure and pay.
Excluded: needs a Microsoft 365 licence.

tradeoffs: Adds another vendor (Resend) to sign up with, secure and pay.

alternatives.why_not: GitHub Actions is preferred because widely used, with free minutes for small teams.
GitLab.com scores lower on cost (2.9 against 5.0, priorities.cost is 2), which accounts for 3.9 of the 10.7-point gap.

alternatives.why_not: Excluded: needs a host with its own build-from-git pipeline.

assumptions: Priced for 50,000 monthly active users (the larger of users_at_launch and users_12_months), interpolated between list-price anchors in the knowledge base.
Prices are list prices of the cheapest region inside the chosen residency zone; taxes are excluded.
Database storage is priced for 200 GB (scale.data_volume_gb_12_months).
The upper bound includes a x1.25 allowance for spiky traffic (not stacked on the staging allowance).
A staging environment is added for a team of 3 or more (x1.1 to x1.3 on core services).
The upper bound is limited to 3 times the lower bound: the components do not all peak in the same month, so the band stays within one order of magnitude.
Firebase Authentication: free tier used at the low end (Free tier: 50,000 MAU on Identity Platform; phone SMS billed separately)
Payment gateway fees (about 2% per transaction), one-time costs, domain names and developer seats are not infrastructure and are excluded.

basis: peak_rps: 0.2 requests per second per concurrent user, x1.5 for spiky traffic, derived
api_instances_at_peak: peak_rps / 250 requests per second per instance, rounded up
the cost band prices hosting by monthly users; per-instance sizing is added to it only when scale.peak_rps is given

warnings.message: EU GDPR: Data processing agreement and SCCs for transfers; DPIA for high-risk processing. The stack keeps data in europe-west1.
The low end of the estimate relies on free tiers: Firebase Authentication (Free tier: 50,000 MAU on Identity Platform; phone SMS billed separately). Check them against the expected traffic.

Make every Stripe charge and refund call idempotent (one idempotency key or order id per attempt) and store processed webhook event ids, so a retry or a repeated webhook never charges or refunds twice.

Card data still falls under PCI DSS even though compliance does not list pci_dss. Use the payment provider's hosted checkout or redirect so card numbers never touch these servers; the merchant then files the short Self-Assessment Questionnaire A instead of a full assessment.
